claims.head: Something has to give
claims.body: The Rangers are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Senators are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Senators’ defense.
claims.call: The Senators keep the Rangers’ chances less dangerous than the league average (a 6.4% chance of scoring on the average shot).

claims.head: The Senators want Batherson away from the big guns
claims.call: The Senators’ L2 (Foegele, Cozens and Batherson) spends at least 35% of its 5-on-5 time against the Rangers’ third line, against about 25% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Senators keep sending Batherson’s line (Foegele, Cozens and Batherson) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Travis Green has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Rangers’ third line is Cuylle, Laba and Tolvanen.
claims.nums: At home: 45% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against third lines, about 25% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Travis Green likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Rangers’ third line.
claims.cite: Matchups · Ottawa home games this season · 6 games, 34 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

With no line matching, this group would face third lines about 25% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

claims.head: Expect a grind
claims.call: The game’s pace score is below 95, slower than either team’s usual.
claims.see: Fewer than 63 shots between them at 5-on-5, on goal or wide, which usually means 53 or fewer shots on goal on the scoreboard.
claims.body: The Rangers play some of the league’s slowest games, and so do the Senators. We think this one is even quieter than either team’s usual.

notes.text: Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 36% of the team’s shorthanded time in 12 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 23% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Jordan Spence has started killing penalties: on the ice for 33% of the team’s shorthanded time in 11 games, up from 4% last season.

stakes: The Rangers go in second in the Metropolitan with 15 points, the Senators tied for second in the Atlantic with 14 points.

OTT.head: Advantage, the Senators
OTT.body: Ottawa has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Rangers’ way back in is keeping shots to a minimum.

NYR.head: A tough matchup for the Rangers
NYR.body: Ottawa has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Rangers can pull it off if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
paras: The Rangers come in at 7-4-1, the Senators at 7-4-0.

It’s strength against strength: the Rangers are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Senators are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. At home, Travis Green likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Rangers’ third line.

items.text: The Senators are newly without Linus Ullmark and Thomas Chabot, and have been without William Eklund since Oct 8. Jonas Johansson is expected to start.
Mika Zibanejad is one point from passing Walt Tkaczuk for sixth on the Rangers’ all-time scoring list.
